title: Security Best Practices

body.text: Security rules when using AI to write code:
no secrets in code or prompts · check the dependencies the AI adds · watch for injection at every input point
— the AI writes code fast, but security always needs a human to check.

example: "Before approving: check there's no hardcoded API key, where new dependencies come from, and whether inputs are validated"

title: Codex Advanced recap

body.text: multi-step work, environment config, CI/CD, TDD, review, and security
— the goal isn't for the AI to replace you, but to shift your time to what humans do best: design, decide, and review.

example: "Final challenge: set up AGENTS.md + an environment for your real repo, then run 3 tasks in parallel this week"

question: Which is a correct security rule?

options.text: Never put secrets in code or prompts
Pasting API keys in prompts is fine, it's convenient
The AI already handles all security itself

question: When the AI adds a new dependency, what should you do?

options.text: Check its source and trustworthiness before approving
Trust the AI and install it right away

question: What's the real goal of agentic coding?

options.text: Shift human time to design, decisions, and review
Write the most code in the world

question: What's the most important security best practice?

options.text: Embed secret keys in public code
Don't expose secret keys, and check code and permissions before use

question: What's the summary of using Codex advanced safely?

options.text: Always plan, test, review, and mind security
